newsitem.title: USA: Millicom stock up after spin-off announced.
newsitem.headline: Millicom stock up after spin-off announced.

text.p: Millicom International Cellular SA's stock climbed more than 18 percent Tuesday after the global cellular phone company announced a restructuring, including the spin-off of its Asian operations.
In addition to spinning off its Asian operations into a separate, publicly listed company, Millicom said it will consider partners or buyers for its Latin American operations.
The Luxembourg-based company concentrates on providing cellular service in countries with limited wire-based telephone phone service and rapid economic development, such as Costa Rica and Vietnam.
The company said it also plans a share repurchase programme.

"We consider that there is substantial value within Millicom's operations which is currently not reflected in the company's stock price," company President Jay Metcalfe said in a statement. "The plan will allow investors to clearly evaluate each part of the business."
Millicom stock rose $6.50 to $42 in late morning trading on Nasdaq. Its 52-week high was $51.25.
Millicom said all the transactions would take place in 1997 and would be tax-free or substantially tax-free.

The company plans to rename itself Millicom SA, with cellular phone operations and interests in Russia, the Baltics, Luxembourg and Africa; its Multinational Automated Clearing House SA subsidiary; and new ventures.
The company lost $18.1 million, or 38 cents per share, on sales of $215.6 million in 1996.
